lesson.title: Check in with someone you love
lesson.scenario: Fattoush and Knafeh catch up at home. Learn a casual check-in, say how you feel, and ask the other person back.

steps.instruction: Fattoush checks in with Knafeh. Respond as Knafeh: you are well.

prompt.meaning: How are you doing? (casual check-in to Knafeh)

answers.rationale: This describes a feminine speaker; you are taking Knafeh’s role.
This answers the check-in about Knafeh himself.
This describes the day; the task asks how Knafeh himself feels.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Ana mnīḥ answers about Knafeh himself. The lesson’s question is a casual check-in.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: Compare the speaker, listener, and intended meaning.
evaluation.retryHint: Use ana and Knafeh’s form of “well.”

steps.instruction: You have answered Knafeh. Ask him the same question back.

answers.rationale: This addresses Fattoush, but your listener is Knafeh.
This asks about a third person instead of your listener.
Inta addresses Knafeh and returns the check-in.

evaluation.correctExplanation: W-inta? invites Knafeh to answer without repeating the question.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: Compare the speaker, listener, and intended meaning.
evaluation.retryHint: Your listener is Knafeh: use inta.

steps.instruction: You are checking in with Fattoush. Choose the question addressed to her.

answers.meaning: How are you doing? (casual check-in to Fattoush)
answers.rationale: ʿĀmle marks the question to Fattoush.

answers.meaning: How are you doing? (casual check-in to Knafeh)
answers.rationale: ʿĀmel is the form addressed to Knafeh.

answers.meaning: What did you do today? (to Knafeh)
answers.rationale: This asks for completed activities and uses masculine address.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Shū ʿāmle? changes the address form for Fattoush.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: Compare the speaker, listener, and intended meaning.
evaluation.retryHint: Listen for the ending of ʿāmle.

steps.instruction: Answer as Fattoush: you are a little tired.

prompt.meaning: How are you doing? (casual check-in to Fattoush)

answers.rationale: Ktīr makes the tiredness strong, changing “a little.”
This describes Knafeh; Fattoush uses taʿbāne.
The description matches Fattoush and keeps the degree mild.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Ana taʿbāne shwayy preserves both Fattoush’s self-description and “a little.”
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: Compare the speaker, listener, and intended meaning.

steps.instruction: Fattoush asks how you are doing. Respond as Knafeh: a little tired.

prompt.meaning: How are you doing? (casual check-in to Knafeh)

answers.rationale: This is the feminine self-description, while you are Knafeh.
This describes Knafeh with mild tiredness.
This changes the requested degree to “very.”

evaluation.correctExplanation: Ana taʿbān shwayy is Knafeh’s self-description; shwayy keeps it mild.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: Compare the speaker, listener, and intended meaning.

steps.instruction: Fattoush offers Knafeh a rest. Accept and say you want a little rest.

prompt.meaning: Do you want to rest? (to Knafeh)

answers.meaning: Yes, I want to rest a little.
answers.rationale: Āh accepts; biddi artāḥ expresses the speaker’s wish.
This declines the offer; the task asks you to accept.
This reports completed activities instead of accepting the offer.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Āh, biddi artāḥ shwayy accepts and says what Knafeh wants now.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: Compare the speaker, listener, and intended meaning.
evaluation.retryHint: Accept first, then say what you want.

steps.instruction: A new check-in: respond as Fattoush that you are well.

prompt.meaning: How are you doing? (casual check-in to Fattoush)

answers.rationale: This is Knafeh’s self-description; you are Fattoush.
This says you are tired, changing the requested meaning.
This describes Fattoush as well.

evaluation.correctExplanation: Ana mnīḥa changes the self-description to fit Fattoush in this new exchange.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: Compare the speaker, listener, and intended meaning.

steps.instruction: You are Knafeh. After answering, return the check-in to Fattoush.

answers.rationale: This addresses Knafeh, but Fattoush is your listener.
Inti addresses Fattoush and keeps the check-in going.

answers.meaning: Yes, I want to rest a little.
answers.rationale: This asks for rest rather than returning the question.

evaluation.correctExplanation: W-inti? completes the exchange by inviting Fattoush to answer.
evaluation.incorrectExplanation: Compare the speaker, listener, and intended meaning.

lesson.unitTitle: Everyday conversations with someone you love

introduction.goal: Check in, say how you feel, and keep a short exchange going.

line.meaning: How are you doing? (casual check-in to Knafeh)
Do you want to rest? (to Knafeh)
Yes, I want to rest a little.

expressions.meaning: How are you doing? (casual check-in to Knafeh)
How are you doing? (casual check-in to Fattoush)

introduction.usageNote: Start with a casual check-in, answer about yourself, then invite the other person to answer. Shū ʿāmel? addresses Knafeh; shū ʿāmle? addresses Fattoush. In this scene it functions as “How are you doing?”; context can also make it a question about what someone is doing. Ana means “I”: Knafeh describes himself with mnīḥ or taʿbān; Fattoush uses mnīḥa or taʿbāne. Shwayy means “a little,” while ktīr means “very” in these descriptions. W-inta? returns the question to Knafeh; w-inti? returns it to Fattoush. Keep the listener and speaker separate when choosing a form.
introduction.dialectNote: Urban Palestinian teaching target. The casual check-in choice follows Palestinian-speaker feedback relayed and clarified by the owner on September 30, 2026. No universal claim about every Palestinian greeting is made. Feminine address and composed exchange are AI-assisted drafts; no native-expert review. Keep transliteration available: ʿ = ع; ā/ī/ū are long vowels. Jordanian alternatives are not introduced here.
introduction.recordingNote: No reviewed recordings yet. Six dialogue turns above are the revised script. Keep each speaker/address form and exact transcript; no native-speaker review is claimed. Browser/device speech remains an optional preview.

teachingCards.title: Start with a casual check-in

phrase.meaning: How are you doing? (casual check-in to Knafeh)

teachingCards.note: This scene uses the question as a greeting to Knafeh. The response tells him how you feel.

teachingCards.title: Answer about yourself
teachingCards.note: Ana identifies the speaker. This form describes Knafeh; Fattoush says mnīḥa.

teachingCards.title: Give a little detail
teachingCards.note: Fattoush is describing herself, so taʿbāne has a feminine ending. Shwayy keeps the tiredness mild.

teachingCards.title: Keep the conversation going
teachingCards.note: You do not need to repeat the whole question. Inti addresses Fattoush; inta addresses Knafeh.

teachingCards.title: Check in with Fattoush

phrase.meaning: How are you doing? (casual check-in to Fattoush)

teachingCards.note: The person you address changes the ending: ʿāmel to Knafeh, ʿāmle to Fattoush.

teachingCards.title: Say what you need

phrase.meaning: Yes, I want to rest a little.

teachingCards.note: Biddi marks what the speaker wants. Reuse shwayy to ask for a little rest.
